evidence.AC1: POST /todos with {"title":"past","dueDate":"2026-10-14"} returned 201 with dueDate "2026-10-14". A todo created without dueDate returned 201 with dueDate null. The date is a plain YYYY-MM-DD string with no time.
evidence.AC2: PATCH /todos/2 {"dueDate":"2026-09-01"} returned 200 and the date changed. PATCH {"dueDate":null} returned 200 with dueDate null. A later PATCH that only changed the title left dueDate unchanged.
evidence.AC3: POST /todos with dueDate 2026-02-30, 15.10.2026, foo, 2026-13-01 and 20261015 each returned 400 with an error message. PATCH with dueDate 2026-02-30 also returned 400.
evidence.AC4: Today is 2026-10-15 UTC. I created todos due yesterday, today and tomorrow, one with no due date, and one past-due todo that I then marked done. GET /todos?overdue=true returned only the past-due not-done todos: id 1 (due 2026-10-14) and id 2 (due 2026-09-01). The todos due today, with no due date, and done were excluded. The unfiltered GET /todos returned all five.
evidence.AC5: At http://localhost:3000/ each todo that has a due date showed it as <time>: 2026-10-14, 2026-09-01, 2026-10-15 and 2026-10-01. The todo without a due date showed none.
evidence.AC6: On the list page, 'past' (due 2026-10-14) and 'future2' (due 2026-09-01) showed the text 'überfällig'. 'today', 'none' and the done 'pastdone' (due in the past) did not show it.
evidence.AC7: The page has a checkbox labelled 'nur überfällige'. After I clicked it, the list showed only 'past' and 'future2', both marked überfällig. The other three todos were hidden.
